title: What, Who, and When: Structured Harm Assessment for Mental Health Safety via Short Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2611.33263v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The growing use of large language models (LLMs) for mental health support raises important safety concerns. Existing guard models primarily identify categories of harmful content, often overlooking the context needed to determine an appropriate response. We introduce a clinically grounded taxonomy that characterizes harm along three dimensions: what the harm is, who is involved, and when it occurs. It further separates harm characterization from intervention decisions, thus enabling safety policies to be specified outside the model weights through explicit, clinician-curated instructions that can be updated and audited. We validate the taxonomy with expert clinicians and validate a panel of LLM judges to scale annotation. Relabeling public benchmarks in this taxonomy shows that they rarely contain harm directed at the user, which accounts for nearly half of the harm in real conversations. translated_title: 什么、谁与何时：基于短推理的心理健康安全性结构化危害评估
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在心理健康支持中的日益广泛应用引发了重要的安全担忧。现有的护栏模型主要识别有害内容的类别，往往忽略了判断适当响应所需的上下文。我们引入了一个基于临床的分类体系，从三个维度刻画危害：危害是什么、涉及谁、何时发生。该体系进一步将危害刻画与干预决策分离，从而使安全策略能够通过明确、由临床医生策划、可更新且可审计的指令在模型权重之外进行规定。我们通过专家临床医生验证了该分类体系，并验证了一个由LLM评判者组成的评审团以实现标注的规模化。使用该分类体系对公开基准进行重新标注的结果显示，这些基准很少包含针对用户的危害，而这类危害在真实对话中占近一半。随后，我们训练了MindGuard2，一个35B-A3B的基于推理的模型。
tldr: 该论文提出基于临床的“什么、谁、何时”三维危害分类体系，将危害刻画与干预决策分离，使心理健康安全策略可在模型权重之外通过可更新、可审计的临床医生指令进行配置，并据此训练出短推理安全评估模型MindGuard2。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a clinically grounded "what, who, and when" taxonomy that separates harm characterization from intervention decisions, enabling updatable and auditable safety policies outside model weights, and trains MindGuard2 for mental health safety assessment via short reasoning.
